newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: HOLLARD BUYS CRUSADER LIFE FOR 18 MLN RAND.
newsitem.headline: HOLLARD BUYS CRUSADER LIFE FOR 18 MLN RAND.

text.p: South African insurer Hollard Insurance Group said on Thursday that it would buy Crusader Life Ltd for about 18 million rand.
Hollard Life managing director Peter Laburn said in a statement the firm would pay 18 million rand for all Crusader's preference shares and 0.5 million rand for the ordinary shares.
All Crusader's businesses will be transferred to Hollard Life, except the Equity Linked Life Annuity business which will be placed with Southern Life.

Hollard is one of South Africa's largest independent insurance groups with combined assets of nearly one billion rand. Crusader had been placed under provisional curatorship in 1993 and also placed under judicial management.
The deal is still subject to Supreme Court and shareholder approval.

Laburn said the amount paid to ordinary shareholders was small, but he added that those shares were effectively worthless as preference shareholders have claims of more than 34 million rand that rank ahead of the ordinary shareholders.
Crusader is also involved in litigation, but Hollard said it would pay 2.1 million rand to the Top Dog Consortium to settle a dispute.
"The deal will be a major relief to Crusader policy holders who have lived with uncertainty for the last three years," Laburn said.
